meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-19 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: James Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Connor Liu (Redwood CSM), Marta Reyes (SilverStream Head of ML), Ethan Cole (SilverStream Infra Lead), Lina Park (SilverStream Security), Raj Patel (Product)
summary: Discovery for Dedicated capacity. Customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive inference, needs isolation, burst to hosted for traffic spikes, and clear scaling and SLAs. They asked about GPU types (A100/H100), autoscale/burst behavior, VPC/KMS controls, benchmarking plan and pricing. Agreed next steps: pricing, SOC2/network docs, perf benchmark scheduling.
topics: GPU types, quantization, and cost tradeoffs
Security controls: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
transcript:
00:00 James Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. Intro — I'm James on the account, Priya is our solutions engineer, Connor from CS. quick agenda: understand current stack, workloads, and whether Dedicated makes sense.
00:18 Marta Reyes: Great thanks. We run SilverStream's inference for our risk-scoring and alerts. latency is the big one, sub-150ms p50 for short prompts, and cost is still important.
00:34 Ethan Cole: Our infra is in GCP, VPC w/ private routing, and we want dedicated GPUs but tightly controlled network egress.
00:45 Priya Shah: Got it. A couple clarifying q's — are these real-time API calls or batch? what's QPS?
00:52 Marta Reyes: Mostly real-time, spikes around 200-400 QPS during market open, average 60 QPS. Some batch overnight for re-scoring.
01:07 Priya Shah: Okay that maps well to Redwood Dedicated. We provide reserved GPU pools, isolation via private deployment in your VPC or a customer VPC peering model, and burst-to-hosted or burst-to-burstpool options.
01:22 Ethan Cole: Burst-to-hosted — is that sending us to Redwood public? We have data residency concerns.
01:29 James Ortega: Right — for SilverStream we'd recommend a controlled burst path. Two options: 1) burst to a Redwood-hosted pool with strict tenancy and contractual controls; 2) allow controlled burst only to a secondary dedicated pool in another region you control. We can discuss encryption and data retention on the path.
01:48 Lina Park: We need KMS integration and no plaintext logs leaving our VPC. How does Redwood handle KMS/HSM?
01:55 Priya Shah: We support customer-managed KMS for keys in Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS via our private control plane. Audit logs can be forwarded into your SIEM. We'll include the SOC2 + architecture doc.
02:10 Raj Patel: What's your recommended GPU? We looked at A100 vs H100 vs 8-bit quantized instances.
02:18 Priya Shah: H100 gives better perf for many transformer workloads; A100 still cost-effective. We often recommend mixed pools: H100 for low-latency critical routes and A100 or 8-bit quantized models for background tasks. Quantization can reduce cost significantly but some QA needed.
02:35 Marta Reyes: For our models we may use a LM-7b variant and some 70b for heavy ops. We can't break latency budget.
02:42 Priya Shah: Understood — our Dedicated product supports model pinning and kernel selection; you can pin model versions and we handle kernel selection and batching automatically. We also have continuous batching heuristics but you can tune for lower latency.
02:58 Ethan Cole: Autoscaling — how quick is scale up? spikes of 300->600 QPS could last 10-15 mins.
03:06 Priya Shah: We support vertical and horizontal autoscale; scale-up depends on reserved capacity headroom. For fast spikes we recommend a burst pool (reserved but idle nodes) or warm standbys. For extreme short bursts we can route to hosted as a fallthrough. Typical scale-up to add a new instance ~3-7 minutes depending on instance type and region; warm pools drop that to under 60s for adding capacity to the routing layer.
03:34 James Ortega: And SLA perspective — Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs for enterprise tiers. We can include the SLA terms in the contract.
03:43 Marta Reyes: Cost — how do you price Dedicated? flat per-GPU + usage?
03:49 James Ortega: Typically reserved capacity is a monthly commit per GPU SKU plus optional overage. Pricing sheet I'll share. There are also autoscale and burst pricing options.
04:02 Ethan Cole: Is there support for private control plane in our GCP project?
04:07 Priya Shah: Yes we support private control plane / VPC deployments and on-prem variants. For VPC we'll peer and place inference nodes in a dedicated subnet; control plane comms can be tunneled via private link or customer-managed VPN.
04:19 Lina Park: Regarding data retention and logs — we need 7 years of audit logs for certain flows. Can logs be exported to our GCS/S3 with encryption at rest?
04:28 Priya Shah: Yes logs can be exported and encrypted using customer keys. We'll provide sample logging retention configs.
04:36 Marta Reyes: Benchmarking — we want to run a realistic benchmark. We'll share token profile and QPS and want Redwood to run a benchmark on a mirrored workload.
04:44 Priya Shah: Perfect — we do joint benchmark runs. We'll need a perf test account and sample payloads. Expect an initial report with p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost-per-1k tokens.
04:56 Raj Patel: Anyone asked about model fallbacks — if a big model is unavailable, can we fallback to smaller model automatically?
05:03 Priya Shah: Yes, smart routing can fallback to pinned variants. You can define policies per route: latency threshold, cost threshold, region preference.
05:12 Marta Reyes: Security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, IP allowlist, penetration testing?
05:19 James Ortega: All supported. We can share our compliance pack; we've done enterprise pentests and have SAML SSO, OIDC, RBAC and audit trails.
05:31 Ethan Cole: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? Could that be shared between tenants?
05:37 Priya Shah: For Dedicated the KV cache is tenant-isolated. We also support prefix caching to reduce repetition cost. For multi-tenant hosted offerings caches are shared but sandboxed; for your Dedicated fleet everything is isolated.
05:50 Marta Reyes: Ok, two more things: model updates and rollouts — we need canary + A/B and rollback.
05:57 Priya Shah: Rollouts supported — canaries, A/B, automatic rollback on regression with eval hooks. You can bind evals to prompt sets.
06:06 Connor Liu: quick note — I'll follow up with onboarding checklist; CS will own pilot success metrics.
06:12 Marta Reyes: Great. Any blockers on networking?
06:16 Ethan Cole: We use private org-wide peering and strict egress rules, so we'd need detailed architecture.
06:22 Priya Shah: We'll include network diagrams. For peering we'll need a list of subnets and IP ranges.
06:28 Marta Reyes: For the benchmark, target SLA is p95 < 300ms and p50 < 120ms for our 7b model, cost target to be within 30% of our current infra.
06:38 James Ortega: Noted — that's helpful. We'll mirror that in the perf plan.
06:42 Raj Patel: Any known perf delta between A100 and H100 for the 7b?
06:46 Priya Shah: H100 tends to shave off 10-30% latency on many attention kernels; real numbers depend on sequence length and batching. We'll include both in the benchmark.
07:00 Marta Reyes: Questions from procurement — contract length and renewal?
07:05 James Ortega: Typical reserved terms are 12-36 months with volume discounts; we'll template a 12-month pilot and then scale.
07:12 Ethan Cole: Network ACL and egress — will your support team ever need to access nodes?
07:18 Priya Shah: Support access can be brokered through a bastion in your project or via read-only logs export; we treat support access as ephemeral and auditable.
07:28 Marta Reyes: We've seen noisy tokenization differences across providers — does Redwood provide deterministic tokenization and explainability?
07:36 Priya Shah: Tokenization is model-dependent; we provide tooling to surface token counts and sample outputs. For evals we can run controlled prompts.
07:44 Raj Patel: What about maintenance windows and patching?
07:49 Priya Shah: Patching is scheduled with advance notice; Dedicated customers can opt into blackout windows. Critical security patches are rolled out with high priority and we coordinate.
07:58 Marta Reyes: Ok what's the timeline for a pilot?
08:02 James Ortega: If we get the perf profile and traffic sample by Friday (2026-08-21) we can schedule a benchmark the week of 2026-08-24 and have a pilot provisioned within 2-3 weeks.
08:13 Ethan Cole: Sounds good. Any other questions?
08:16 Raj Patel: Competitors — we've talked to Bedrock and Anthropic. how do you differentiate?
08:21 James Ortega: Our differentiation is production-first runtime with unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private, clear observability, and cost controls like batching, KV cache and quantization recommendations. We'll share comparative notes.
08:33 Marta Reyes: Good. Let's recap next steps.
08:36 Connor Liu: Recap: Redwood sends pricing + SOC2/network docs; SilverStream shares token profile and perf test account; schedule benchmark week of 8/24.
08:48 James Ortega: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
09:00 [Call ends — total 55m aprox.]
references: SOC2 & Network Architecture: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-arch.pdf (to be attached)
